title: SLO crediting and progressive failover-delay hysteresis policy for multi-region endpoints
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Goal: Define a deterministic, implementable policy for SLO crediting, cross-region error-budget borrowing, and progressive failover delay with hysteresis to avoid oscillatory regional eject/retry behavior for multi-region model endpoints. This ticket codifies the math, thresholds, and lifecycle actions (evict/soft-fallback/harden) and produces an operational playbook + simulation results for rollout. The policy must balance availability and request-quality guarantees for latency-sensitive routes while limiting cross-region cost exposure.
acceptance_criteria: A human-readable SLO crediting spec that maps per-endpoint SLIs (p50/p95 latency, request_quality score, availability) to a single error-budget currency and defines borrow/repay rules
Hysteresis algorithm and timer parameters documented with rationale and example timelines demonstrating avoidance of flip-flop during transient spikes
Circuit-breaker thresholds derived from credit levels and per-variant priority matrix; implementation knobs enumerated for runtime team
Simulation workbook (CSV + notebook link) showing behavior across 1000 synthetic traffic bursts and at least 3 real traffic traces
Runbook steps for operators to execute regional evacuation, manual override, and postmortem checklist
Implementation-ready RFC and a staging PR for runtime that wire up metrics and a feature flag
decisions: Use a unified error-budget currency 'EBC' that combines weighted latency and request-quality deficits. Weighting: request_quality=0.6, latency=0.4 by default (modifiable per-route).
Cross-region borrowing is allowed only up to 30% of local EBC and must be repaid within a configurable repay_window (default: 6 hours).
Progressive failover delay: regions do not immediately eject; apply staged delays (soft-fallback -> partial-evict -> hard-evict) with increasing hysteresis windows [5min, 20min, 60min].
Hysteresis semantics: once a region escalates, it must pass a cool-down recovery window (slightly longer than the escalation) before being eligible for reintake to avoid oscillation.
Circuit-breaker engages when EBC falls below 10% and sustained SLI breach persists > 90s; shedding policy respects tenant priority bands (gold/silver/free).
KV-cache-sensitive routes should decrease EBC burn rate multiplier when a KV cache hit is observed (to avoid penalizing cached requests).
notes: Rationale: Past incidents showed rapid eject/restart cycles during noisy infra events in eu-west and us-east, causing extra cross-region tail latency and cost. Hysteresis reduces churn and gives autoscaler time to stabilize.
Trade-offs: Longer hysteresis reduces flapping but increases exposure to degraded region behavior; the staged approach allows for incremental protection while preserving capacity.
Metrics required: per-region p50/p95/p99 latency, request_quality (eval promptset scoring), availability ratio, EBC balance, cross-region borrow ledger.
Open question: whether to make repay_window dynamic based on traffic volume — deferred to runtime simulation step.
